top_strength: Genuinely strong returning-customer moment — he noticed the prior move in the system, said 'welcome back, we're definitely excited to work with you again,' and pulled the ~20-box count off that old move to help the customer answer a question he'd already said he couldn't answer. He then defused it well: 'that's not a number we're gonna hold you to.'
coaching_note: This call collected information and delivered nothing. Jespah gathered decent move details and then handed the entire value pitch to an email — no rate, no what's-included, no clock, no No Worries, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee, no estimate, no booking attempt. A returning customer who is already sold on Einstein is the easiest booking on the board, and Jespah let him hang up unbooked with a to-do item. Next call: once the probe is done, say 'great, let me walk you through pricing real quick' and deliver Sections 3-7 live, then ask for the date. The email should confirm what was already agreed, not carry the pitch. Second priority: he skipped the Save Your Ass speech even after Nicolas volunteered that he stages boxes by the door to speed the crew up — that is a customer handing you the opener.
phone_presence_notes: Friendly and easy to talk to with real warmth in the 'welcome back' moment, but heavily padded with filler and dead air ('give me a couple of seconds here', 'let me see if I have any other questions') and he let the customer's move-day prep story pass with a flat 'Oh, cool' instead of building on it.
